title: A source-level guide explains what LangGraph builds under its abstractions
friendlyTitle: A practical guide opens the box inside LangGraph
summary: Tamir Dresher traced LangGraph 1.2.12 from its Runnable interface through channels, reducers, compiled graphs and deep agents, using pinned offline examples that readers can reproduce. The guide argues that graphs, ReAct agents and deep agents share the same Pregel execution core with different configuration.
friendlySummary: The guide shows how LangGraph stores state, runs steps and builds larger agents from the same core system. It includes fixed software versions and example code that can run without a live model.
whyItMatters: Understanding the machinery beneath an agent framework makes debugging state, retries and parallel work less mysterious. Builders can use the guide to decide where an abstraction helps and where direct control or instrumentation is needed.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Agents are easier to fix when developers understand what happens under the framework. The guide can help teams find state and workflow problems instead of treating the system like magic.
